headline: High: CrewAI’s shared workspace and broad egress can collide with nullclaw’s MCP, durable memory, and secret-bearing CRM surfaces, creating leakage and action-conflict risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; nullclaw exposes workspace files, webhooks, MCP, and browser/tool channels. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if one agent consumes the other’s file or tool output as trusted content. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF CrewAI outputs text into a shared workspace that nullclaw later parses as instructions
IF nullclaw ingests CrewAI-generated files or webhook payloads without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic parsing of peer-generated files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts
Require manual review before tool execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers around shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and broad model-provider/tool egress, while nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, and audit logs. If they share a workspace or credentials store, sensitive data can flow from CrewAI into nullclaw’s broader channel set or vice versa. The blast radius includes secrets exfiltration, so uncertainty should not be down-ranked.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or config directory
IF either agent is configured to forward file contents or logs to external model providers
mitigations: Place secrets in separate per-agent vaults
Mount distinct workspaces with no cross-read access
Rotate any shared API keys before co-running
Disable log export for secret-bearing sessions
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent credential isolation in the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; nullclaw also modifies git state and uses MCP. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because CrewAI lacks default self-isolation and nullclaw’s session scope spans channels/accounts, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or workspace
IF nullclaw’s git actions and CrewAI’s file writes occur concurrently
mitigations: Use separate repositories or worktrees
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable git mutation in one agent
Run each agent in its own container volume
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from delegated subagents, and nullclaw’s tool-use pattern includes delegate, schedule, git, and web actions. If nullclaw treats CrewAI output as authoritative, an upstream hallucination can cascade into downstream actions or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, but the blast radius is bounded by operator oversight.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes CrewAI-produced text without an explicit verification step
IF CrewAI-generated recommendations are used to trigger nullclaw scheduling, web, or git actions
mitigations: Require a human approval step before actions
Cross-check critical facts against a second source
Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted inputs
Restrict nullclaw to read-only mode for CrewAI-fed tasks
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is documented as handling developer-passed crew data and API keys, while nullclaw explicitly touches audit logs, workspace files, and multiple secret classes. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge, especially because nullclaw’s docs expose broad network and storage surfaces. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through both agents in the same workflow
IF one agent retains logs or workspace files longer than the other
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable retention of audit logs for sensitive runs
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Document residency and retention for each agent
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
